name: 2. Semantic HTML and Modern Document Engineering

quiz.question: What is the primary purpose of `<!DOCTYPE html>` at the top of an HTML5 document?
options: It instructs the browser to parse the document in modern HTML standards mode rather than legacy quirks mode
It registers the domain in DNS
quiz.explanation: The DOCTYPE declaration switches browsers into standards mode so layout and parsing follow modern HTML specifications.

quiz.question: Which set of HTML elements are all void elements (cannot contain child content and have no closing tags)?
options: img, br, hr, input, meta, link
quiz.explanation: Void elements such as img, br, hr, input, meta, and link cannot have child nodes or closing tags.

quiz.question: When should you choose `<article>` instead of `<section>`?
options: Whenever you need a generic styling wrapper
When the content is a self-contained composition (such as a blog post, news item, or course card) that makes sense independently
quiz.explanation: `<article>` represents an independent, self-contained composition, whereas `<section>` groups thematically related content.

quiz.question: Why is a native `<button type="button">` preferred over `<div onclick="...">` for interactive actions?
options: Div elements cannot be styled with CSS
A native button provides built-in keyboard activation (Enter/Space), focusability, and button semantics for assistive technologies
Buttons automatically submit GET requests without JavaScript
quiz.explanation: Native semantic controls deliver keyboard support, focus management, and accessibility semantics out of the box.

quiz.question: What is the recommended `alt` attribute value for a purely decorative image that adds no informational value?
options: Set `alt=""` (an empty string) so assistive technologies skip announcing it unnecessarily
quiz.explanation: An empty `alt=""` tells screen readers the image is decorative; omitting `alt` entirely may cause them to read the filename.

quiz.question: In an HTML form, what is the difference between `method="get"` and `method="post"`?
options: POST encrypts data without needing HTTPS; GET does not
GET appends form parameters to the URL query string (good for bookmarkable searches), while POST sends data in the request body (good for state-changing operations)
GET is only for file uploads
POST cannot be used with `<input type="email">`
quiz.explanation: GET encodes parameters into the URL for idempotent retrieval; POST sends data in the HTTP body, though HTTPS is still required for encryption.

quiz.question: In the Constraint Validation API, how do you clear a custom validation error previously set with `input.setCustomValidity("...")`?
quiz.explanation: A control remains invalid until `setCustomValidity("")` is called with an empty string.

quiz.question: Which HTML attributes improve accessibility in a data table by explicitly linking header cells to their row or column cells?
options: `<th>` with `scope="col"` or `scope="row"` (and `<caption>` for the table title)
quiz.explanation: Using `<th>` with `scope` and `<caption>` allows screen readers to announce column and row headers for each data cell.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of `<link rel="canonical" href="...">` in the `<head>`?
options: It redirects users automatically to another domain
It indicates the preferred URL for a page when multiple URLs serve substantially identical content
It blocks search engines from crawling the page
quiz.explanation: Canonical links help search engines consolidate duplicate or parameterized URLs onto one preferred URL.

quiz.question: What are the four core principles of WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines)?
quiz.explanation: WCAG organizes accessibility around POUR: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, and Robust.
